content.overview: The schedules form part of the statutory architecture of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996. The First, Second and Third Schedules reproduce Convention instruments; the Fourth Schedule contains model arbitrator-fee figures; and the Fifth, Sixth and Seventh Schedules concern disclosures, disclosure form and specified ineligibility relationships for arbitrator appointment.
content.glance: Statutory schedules must be read with the sections that expressly invoke them and with later amendments and current commencement status.
content.study:
Schedule 1 — Convention on the Recognition and Enforcement of Foreign Arbitral Awards (New York Convention): read with section 44.

Schedule 2 — Protocol on Arbitration Clauses: historical Convention material within Part II.

Schedule 3 — Convention on the Execution of Foreign Arbitral Awards: historical Convention material within Part II.

Schedule 4 — Fourth Schedule: model fee schedule referenced by section 11(14), subject to the statutory conditions and exceptions.

Schedule 5 — Fifth Schedule: grounds giving rise to justifiable doubts as to the independence or impartiality of an arbitrator, relevant to section 12.

Schedule 6 — Sixth Schedule: disclosure form and particulars for section 12 disclosures.

Schedule 7 — Seventh Schedule: relationships/categories that render a person ineligible for appointment as arbitrator under section 12(5), subject to the statutory proviso and party-agreement requirements.

sections.heading: Convention schedules
sections.body: The First to Third Schedules contain Convention instruments and must be distinguished from the operative domestic procedural provisions.

sections.heading: Fee schedule
sections.body: The Fourth Schedule supplies the statutory model fee structure where section 11(14) makes it relevant.

sections.heading: Independence and impartiality schedules
sections.body: The Fifth, Sixth and Seventh Schedules operate with section 12 and should be read together with the statutory disclosure and ineligibility framework.

examples.title: Section 12 application
examples.body: Where the statutory disclosure regime is engaged, identify the relevant Fifth Schedule circumstances, use the Sixth Schedule disclosure form where required, and separately test the Seventh Schedule ineligibility rule.

hypotheticals.question: Are the Fifth and Seventh Schedules interchangeable?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. The Fifth Schedule concerns circumstances giving rise to justifiable doubts as to independence or impartiality; the Seventh Schedule addresses statutory ineligibility, subject to its proviso.

rows.left: Circumstances relevant to justifiable doubts as to independence or impartiality.
rows.right: Specified relationships/categories producing statutory ineligibility under section 12(5), subject to the proviso.

misconceptions.trap: Treating every schedule as an independent substantive cause of action.
misconceptions.correction: Schedules operate through the statutory sections that invoke them.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should the schedules be used?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Identify the section invoking the schedule, state the schedule's statutory function, and apply its contents only within that statutory framework.
